Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City OFFICE OF THE SECRETARY Opinion No. 32 s. 2011 CSUPT SAMUEL R PEREZ, CEO VI Deputy Chief for Administration BUREAU OF FIRE PROTECTION Rm 618, 145 Union Square Condominium 15th Avenue, Cubao, Quezon City Subject: OPINION ON THE INTENDED RENEWAL OF SURETY BOND OF F/DIRECTOR DANILO F CABRERA (Ret.) Ili Dear Chief Supt Perez: This is in reference to your request for legal opinion on whether Ret.Director Danilo F. Cabrera will be allowed to post again or renew his surety bond in order to enjoy his monthly retirement pension pending the resolution of his administrative case with the Ombudsman. As culled from the records, Ret. Dir. Cabrera retired from the service on 08 May 2008 with the rank of Director after rendering more than 25 years of active service, without any mention of the retirement was optional or compulsory/mandatory, Despite the pendency of an administrative case against him before the Office of the Ombudsman, BFP thru its then Benefits Assistance Section, now Retirement Benefit Section, allowed Ret.Dir. Cabrera to post a Surety Bond in the amount of 10% of the face value of his 3-Year Lump Sum claim, and eventually released the said claim. Hence, the above query. BPF Legal Affairs Service Chief, Supt. Candido of BFP opined that: "xxx the Bond should have sufficient face value covering at least the amount it is sought to be released and that the validity thereof should be up to the termination of the pending administrative case of the retiring personnel. Therefore, this office respectfully submits that since the Surety Bond posted by RETIRED DIRECTOR DANILO R CABRERA cannot be considered as a sufficient safeguard to ensure restitution of any retirement benefits that will be released, renewal thereof should not be allowed." (emphasis supplied) In resolution of the foregoing, this Department concurs with the view of the BFP Legal Affairs Service but with modification. Section 12 of RA 3019 or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act states that "No public officer Shal/ be a//owed to resign or retire pending an investigation, criminal or administrative, or pending a prosecution against him for any offense under this Act or under the provisions of the Revised Pena/ Code on bribery." In the determination of whether to allow the public officer to retire or not presupposes that the public officer has not reached the compulsory or mandatory 1'

12 age of retirement and is availing of an optional one, thereby, giving the department , office, or agency the discretion to grant or deny such application for retirement. Thus, iti will be a different matter if the public officer retiring has reached the compulsory age of retirement. In such a case, there is a need for the concenred department, office, or agency to impose or require pertinent measures in dealing with a retiree with pending administrative cases. Under the present rules, the Head of the department, office, or agency concerned has the responsibility of determining whether to release his retirement benefits, as well as the imposition of necessary safeguards to ensure restitution thereof in the event retiree is found guilty. (Memorandum Circular No. 1-0 on the Revised Circular on Ombudsman Clearance, 24 January 1995) In the case of Ret, CSupt Cabrera, it appears that he was allowed to retire however, without any mention at all if such retirement was optional or mandatory/compulsory. Moreover, he had already received and actually enjoyed his 3-year lump sum retirement benefit despite the pendency of his administrative case with the Ombudsman after being allowed to post a Surety Bond in the amount of 10% of the face value of his 3-year lump sum claim. It is our view that pending the resolution of the administrative case against Ret. CSupt Cabrera, his monthly retirement pension should not be released by BFP, unless Ret. CSupt Cabrera posts a SURETY BOND: in an amount equivalent the 3-Year lump sum claim that he had already received and enjoyed; plus one that will cover his annual retirennent pension to be renewed annually. To our minds, why expose the Government to future problems of unnecessarily spending its resources "recovering" funds when it could verily exercise prudence at the outset, such as the posting of a Surety Bond as discussed, to protect its resources and funds, considering the presence of the "risk of conviction" which, under the law, carries with it a penalty that includes "forfeiture of all benefits?" Thus, the BFP, at its discretion, may institute ways or measures other than a Surety Bond, to ensure that it will be able to readily and sufficiently recover from Ret. CSupt Cabrera all retirement benefits released and issued to him in the event that the latter gets a CONVICTION, considering that under Section 13 of RA 3019, Ret. CSupt Cabrera, having been separated from the service and had received such benefits, is liable to restitute the same to the Government. Thank you very much. Very truly yours, SE E .
